req.title: Update only by author
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden when a user attempts to update a post they did not author.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /<id>/update must return HTTP 403 when a logged-in user who is NOT the post author attempts to update it. We need: (1) a positive case confirming the author CAN update (2xx), (2) a negative case confirming a non-author gets 403, and (3) a boundary/state-transition case covering the exact authorship check boundary (same user id vs different user id). We use pre-loaded data: post id=7 is authored by user id=2 (Anjali/cloud); user id=1 (Rahul/stone) is a non-author. Post id=2 is authored by user id=1 (Rahul/stone). We assert exact status codes (403, 200/302) to catch comparison-operator mutations, and verify the 403 is not 404 or 200 to catch constant mutations.

tests.name: test_author_can_update_own_post_returns_2xx
preconditions: Database is initialised with pre-loaded rows
User Rahul (id=1, password=stone) is the author of post id=2
Rahul is logged in via POST /auth/login
actions: POST /2/update with title='Updated Title', body='Updated body'
expected: Update returns HTTP 302 (redirect to index on success)
trace: blog.py get_post: check_author=True, post[author_id]==g.user[id] -> no abort
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_author_can_update_own_post_returns_2xx():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r_login.status_code == 302
    r_update = client.post('/2/update', data={'title': 'Updated Title', 'body': 'Updated body'})
    assert r_update.status_code == 302
    assert r_update.status_code != 403
    assert r_update.status_code != 404

test_author_can_update_own_post_returns_2xx()

tests.name: test_state_transition_login_then_non_author_update_forbidden
preconditions: Database is initialised with pre-loaded rows
Post id=1 is authored by user id=5 (James)
User Anjali (id=2) is NOT the author of post id=1
System starts in anonymous state
actions: Verify anonymous POST /1/update redirects to login (not 403)
POST /auth/login with username=Anjali, password=cloud to transition to authenticated state
POST /1/update as authenticated non-author to trigger 403
expected: Anonymous update attempt returns HTTP 302 redirect to /auth/login
Authenticated non-author update returns exactly HTTP 403
trace: auth.py login_required: anonymous -> redirect(302); blog.py get_post: non-author -> abort(403)
STC: covers anonymous state (302 redirect) and authenticated-non-author state (403)

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_state_transition_login_then_non_author_update_forbidden():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r_anon = client.post('/1/update', data={'title': 'T', 'body': 'B'})
    assert r_anon.status_code == 302
    assert '/auth/login' in r_anon.headers['Location']
    r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert r_login.status_code == 302
    r_update = client.post('/1/update', data={'title': 'T', 'body': 'B'})
    assert r_update.status_code == 403
    assert r_update.status_code != 302
    assert r_update.status_code != 200
